title: You’ve probably read it before… and just moved on.
paragraphs: You’ve probably read it before… and just moved on.
God said He would send hornets ahead of Israel.

Not angels with flaming swords.
Not earthquakes.
Hornets.
And most people never stop to ask why.
Because if you understand this moment, it will confront the way you think God fights for you.
It was a promise spoken long before Israel ever set foot in the land.
In Exodus 23:28, God declares:
“And I will send hornets before you, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite from before you.”
Read that again.

God didn’t say Israel would overpower them with strength.
He didn’t say strategy would win the land.
He said He would go first… and the enemy would be driven out by something small, relentless, unavoidable.
Imagine it.
You’re a Canaanite farmer. The sun is high. The land is yours—or so you think. Then suddenly the air changes. A low, angry hum fills the silence. Not one insect. Not a few.
A swarm.
They don’t negotiate. They don’t reason. They don’t stop.

They chase you out of your own house.
They drive warriors from fortified cities.
They scatter entire people groups.

No sword raised.
No army marching.
Just terror you can’t control.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
This wasn’t just about insects.
It was about authority.
God was showing Israel—and exposing something deeper in you—that victory was never supposed to come from your strength.
Because if it did, you would take the credit.
And you already do.

You call it your discipline.
Your intelligence.
Your timing.
But God sees the pride behind it.
God saw it.
You knew.
Later, the promise is repeated in Deuteronomy 7:20:
“Moreover the Lord your God will send the hornet among them, until those who are left and hide themselves from you are destroyed.”
Not just exposed.
Hunted.
Even the hidden ones.

The ones behind walls.
The ones pretending safety.
The ones thinking they escaped judgment.
God’s judgment doesn’t lose track.
And then, years later, it happens.
In Joshua 24:12, God reminds them:
“I sent the hornet before you, which drove them out from before you… not by your sword or by your bow.”
Not your sword.
Not your bow.
So why do you still believe your life will be fixed by your effort?
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
This is where it turns.
Because the hornets weren’t just about Canaanites.
They are a mirror.
God still sends things ahead of you.

Conviction you can’t ignore.
Restlessness you can’t silence.
Truth that keeps stinging your conscience.

You try to distract yourself…
But it follows you.

You scroll.
You laugh.
You pretend.
But it comes back.
That’s not random.
That’s mercy.
Because before God removes enemies around you, He confronts the rebellion inside you.
And here’s the part many don’t want to hear—
You are not Israel in the story.
You are the one being driven out.
Sin has made you an enemy of God.
Romans 3:23 says:
“For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God.”
All.
Not some.
Not “bad people.”
You.
And the justice of God doesn’t just pass by sin.
It hunts it down.
Like a swarm you can’t outrun.
But then—
Everything shifts at the cross.
Because the judgment that should have chased you… found Jesus instead.
Isaiah 53:5:
“But He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities… and with His stripes we are healed.”
Read that again.
The wrath didn’t disappear.
It was redirected.
Jesus Christ stepped into your place.
He absorbed what you deserved.
So now, instead of being driven out… you’re invited in.

Not by your strength.
Not by your goodness.
Not by your effort.
But by grace.
And now you stand in a moment just like Israel did.
Two futures in front of you.

You can keep running…
Pretending the conviction will stop…
Hoping the truth won’t catch up to you.
Or you can surrender.
Repent.
Turn.
Because the same God who sends the hornet also opens the door to mercy.
But not forever.
Say it plainly—“I feel the conviction.”
Not for attention.
For honesty.
There are people in your life who are still running, still ignoring what God is doing. Share this with them.
Because there will be a moment when the noise comes back… and you’ll remember this wasn’t coincidence.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—real teaching, real correction, real growth that doesn’t compromise—step into it here:
Because surface-level faith won’t hold when God starts moving.
